News.title: Is the heatwave over? When the hot UK weather will end and latest Met Office forecast
News.content:
BRITAIN has been basking in the summer weather over the past week, with millions filling up paddling pools and heading to the beach to soak up the sun.

With temperatures climbing towards 33C, it’s felt like a holiday at home – but how long will this hot spell last, and will we see more of it later in the month?



Is the heatwave over?

The Met Office has confirmed that high pressure remains firmly in charge of our weather this week, keeping skies clear and the sunshine bright for the majority of the UK.

This means that the current heatwave – a term which has a specific technical definition, based on regional temperature thresholds – is continuing for a little longer.



According to Met Office spokesman Stephen Dixon, the current hot spell will peak midweek, with southern-central England potentially hitting 33C on Wednesday (July 15).

The rest of the country will also enjoy temperatures sitting in the mid-to-high 20s and low 30s.

But things will ease slightly as we approach the weekend, which is when the current “official” heatwave streak is expected to draw to a close.

From Saturday (July 18), a gentle northerly influence will edge in, bringing a slight dip in temperatures that will likely drop many regions just below their official three-day thresholds.

But the Met Office confirms that the high-pressure system isn’t going anywhere yet; the settled summer pattern is set to continue through the weekend, keeping conditions warm, dry, and rain-free in the mid-to-high 20s.

What is the definition of a heatwave?

The Met Office uses strict criteria to officially declare a heatwave – it’s not just about a single hot afternoon.



A heatwave is triggered only when a specific temperature threshold is met or exceeded for three consecutive days.

These thresholds vary across the UK to reflect local climates.

For example, London and the Home Counties have a higher bar of 28C – and even though temperatures have dropped slightly since last week’s highs, recent days have still been hitting that level.

Parts of northern England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland have thresholds set at 25C, which again have been comfortably surpassed in many areas.

As that northerly breeze pulls temperatures down into the mid-20s this weekend, many regions will likely drop just below their official three-day threshold.



When will the next heatwave be?

Looking at the Met Office’s long-range forecast, high pressure is set to remain close to the UK through late July.

While there may be a few summer showers or thunderstorms toward the end of the month, temperatures are expected to stay above average.

The forecast also suggests that between late July and mid-August, we’re likely to see drier, brighter interludes, particularly across the south and southeast, with further hot spells highly possible.

News.title: Hosepipe ban exemptions: The groups that can ignore Temporary Use Bans
News.content:
SOARING summer temperatures have brought on the inevitable return of the dreaded hosepipe ban.

With water suppliers across the country enforcing Temporary Use Bans (TUBs), millions of Brits face £1,000 fines for watering their lawns or washing their cars – but some groups might be legally exempt.



Who is exempt from hosepipe ban rules?

Exemptions are in place to protect groups of people who rely on water for health, safety, and basic welfare.

For example, Blue Badge Holders and the mobility impaired are generally permitted to use a hosepipe if they have severe mobility issues.



Some firms allow exemptions for individuals with a severe disability who find it physically painful or difficult to carry a heavy watering can.

Families on the government’s WaterSure scheme are also widely exempted by suppliers.



To qualify, households must receive certain benefits and have an essential need for high water use, either due to a medical condition or because they have three or more children under the age of 19.

You are also legally allowed to use a hosepipe if it is required to protect the health and welfare of animals.

This includes filling water troughs for livestock, maintaining garden fish ponds, and keeping pets cool.

Customers registered on their water firm’s Priority Services Register (PSR) – for example those who are elderly, have a chronic illness, or use a medical dialyser at home – often receive exemptions.



People on PSR can also receive priority updates during a supply interruption, and free bottled water delivered to the door if their mains water goes off.

Do all water firms offer hosepipe ban exemptions?

Because water companies operate regionally, the rules can vary – while some may opt for blanket exemptions, other suppliers have specific criteria in place.

For example, Cambridge Water say only those with a severe disability who struggle to use a watering can difficult are allowed – rather than a blanket exemption.

To find out the guidelines for your area, head to your firm’s dedicated “Hosepipe Ban” or “Temporary Use Ban (TUB)” section of its website.

Every firm publishes a list of who can and cannot use a hosepipe during a restriction period.



How can you continue tending to your garden?

If you don’t qualify for an exemption, you can still keep your garden thriving without breaking the law or risking a fine.

Hosepipe bans target hoses and sprinklers, so you are completely free to use a traditional watering can as much as you like.

A good tip is to recycle your ‘greywater’ – like bathwater or washing-up water.

Don’t let it go down the drain (as long as it doesn’t contain harsh chemicals); it’s perfect for keeping plants and lawns hydrated.

You can also set a water butt up under your gutter downpipe to capture every drop of rainfall.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

And when you do get the watering can out, water your garden early in the morning or late in the evening.

This ensures the water sinks into the soil rather than evaporating instantly in the midday sun.

News.title: Boy, 11, who died after being hit by lorry is pictured as tributes pour in for ‘precious & caring’ football player
News.content:
'SHINING LIGHT' Boy, 11, who died after being hit by lorry is pictured as tributes pour in for ‘precious & caring’ football player

TRIBUTES have been paid to an 11-year-old footballer who sadly passed away after being hit by a lorry on a quiet country road.

George Dennis was rushed to hospital after he was struck by the HGV on Epping Road, Chipping Ongar, Essex, at around 4.20pm on Friday.



Tragically, despite the best efforts of medics, George was pronounced dead in hospital.

A fundraiser has since been set up to support the 11 year old’s family in the wake of the tragedy.



Tributes to George have begun to flood in with people describing the young lad as: “One of a kind, a shining light, kind, caring, beautiful and far too precious.”

His former football club, Ongar Juniors, also released a public statement which reads: “It is with immense sadness that we share the heartbreaking news that our former and recently returning player, George, tragically lost his life in a road traffic accident.



“George was a talented footballer, a natural leader, and a much-loved member of the Ongar Juniors family.

“Known affectionately as ‘Twinkle Toes’, he will be remembered for his wonderful ability, his huge smile, and the joy he brought to his teammates and coaches.

“Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with George’s family, friends, and everyone affected by this unimaginable loss.”

A 48-year-old man from Derbyshire was arrested at the scene on suspicion of causing serious injuries by dangerous driving.



The suspect was released on bail until September while police continue their investigations.

He has now been re-arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving, cops said.

A police spokesman said at the time: “Officers investigating a fatal collision in Ongar continue to ask for witnesses and dash cam footage.

“We were called at around 4.20pm on Friday 10 July to a collision involving a lorry and a child at Epping Road.

“The child sustained serious injuries and was taken to hospital where, sadly, he died. His family are being supported by specialist officers.



“The lorry driver was arrested at the scene on suspicion of causing serious injuries by dangerous driving.

“The 48-year-old man from Derbyshire has been further arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

“He has been released on bail until mid-September while our investigation continues.

“The road was closed whilst we carried out enquiries at the scene.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The investigation is being led by officers in the Serious Collision Investigation Unit who continue to appeal for witnesses and anyone driving in the vicinity at the time who may have captured footage on dash cam, to contact them.



“If you have any information, CCTV, dash cam or other footage in relation to this incident, then please get in contact with us.”

News.title: Over 3.2million drivers can IGNORE hosepipe ban in UK – avoiding £1,000 fine
News.content:
MILLIONS of UK motorists can ignore the latest hosepipe ban as a result of this little-known rule.

This comes as five major water companies have introduced restrictions to supply across the country.

Large parts of the UK have been placed under hosepipe bans this summer, following record-breaking temperatures and the country’s third successive heatwave.



Yet, those holding a blue badge may not realise they are exempt.



More than 3.2 million blue badge holders in the UK do not need to follow hosepipe restrictions, which prevents residents from using hosepipes for gardening, washing cars, filling swimming pools, and other outdoor water uses.

This is because those with mobility issues may be physically unable to lift, carry or use watering cans to manually tend to their gardens or vehicles.

Forcing individuals with certain disabilities to carry heavy watering cans could also pose a health risk.



As a result, Blue Badge holders are able to continue using hosepipes for their gardens and vehicles – without facing an £1,000 penalty.

However, holders should contact their water supplier first to let them know of their Blue Badge status.

It is also best to receive confirmation from the company as evidence of exemption and some firms may require physical proof, which may include supplying a copy of their blue badge.

Despite exemptions, it is also advised to continue using water responsibly and sparingly.



Other exclusions include those on the Priority Services Register, as well as those who may require the use of a hose for a medical purpose.

News.title: Shock moment pole-dancer FLOODS her apartment after smashing ceiling sprinkler as practice goes horribly wrong
News.content:
THIS is the moment a woman’s attempt to practice her pole-dancing moves goes terribly wrong when the bar hits a sprinkler and floods her home.

Asha Gilbert from Texas, US, attempted to spin on the pole, but it dislodged and knocked a ceiling sprinkler as it fell sideways.



Chaotic footage shows water bursting out of the hole in the ceiling and drenching her Houston apartment.

Water continues to gush as the pole-dancing enthusiast rushes around the room.



The video captures her picking up the phone she had set up to record her dance moves and running for the exit.

Asha later said she had gone into “shock” and was “completely stunned” by the disastrous results.

She said her main concern had been for the safety of her dog.

Both the pooch and owner managed to flee the building unscathed, with firefighters attending the scene.



She had been attempting to follow an instruction video playing on the TV demonstrating some pole-dancing techniques.

Asha later made light of her pole-dancing blunder and shared a video of herself appearing unscathed.

The video shows her sitting on a stool and positioning herself as if she is about to tell her story to a documentary film crew, in a nod to the Netflix documentary trend taking over social media.

The caption said: “POV: Me preparing for the Netflix documentary: Surviving going viral because my pole hit a sprinkler”.

Pole-dancing has become an increasingly popular form of exercise and is no longer solely the domain of strip clubs.



There are now many portable at-home poles for pole-dancing that are marketed as easy to install.

The fiasco highlights the risks of failing to properly install the devices.

The poles, which are specially designed to spin to allow the dancer to execute aerial moves, can cost upwards of £100 to purchase online.

News.title: Teen, 19, dies in hospital after ‘catastrophic’ house fire as heartbroken mum pays tribute to ‘funny and bright lad’
News.content:
FAMILY'S AGONY Teen, 19, dies in hospital after ‘catastrophic’ house fire as heartbroken mum pays tribute to ‘funny and bright lad’

TRIBUTES have been paid to a “bright lad” who tragically died following a “catastrophic” house fire believed to have been started by an e-bike.

Joey Gregory, 19, died in hospital on Thursday last week – nine days after he was injured in the blaze on Redcar Road, Blackpool.



A 13-year-old boy, Coby Keogh, was also injured in the inferno and left in a serious condition in hospital.

Tragically, young Coby passed away on July 5, with his family launching an appeal to raise money for his funeral.



Joey was also rescued from the flames and rushed to the burns intensive care unit at Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester.

He was placed in a medically induced coma with his mum urging her boy to “keep fighting.”

Speaking today in the wake of his death, Joey’s mum Sally Gregory, paid tribute to her son.

She told The Gazette: “We are absolutely devastated, it has been a hell of a nine days. But we had a chance to say goodbye to him and that means everything.

“Not everyone gets the chance to do that and we are not angry, we are surrounded by love.

“He was hilarious, witty, articulate and a very bright lad, he was funny and daft.”



Police and the fire service are working to investigate the cause of the fire, saying they believe it was started by an e-bike.

Blackpool Police said at this time there is believed to be no third party involvement in the tragedy.

Blackpool Police said: “Following a report of a fire within a property on Redcar Road, a 19-year-old man has sadly died.

“Our thoughts remain with his family and loved ones at this devastating time.

“The man’s family are being supported by specially trained officers, and a file will be prepared for the coroner in due course.



“An investigation into the cause of the fire is ongoing between police and the fire and rescue service and there is no third-party involvement.

“At this time, we believe the fire was started by an e-bike.”

News.title: Brit war hero, 49, locked up in ex-Soviet hell jail after painkillers deemed ‘banned drugs’ faces £60k bill to be freed
News.content:
HERO'S PAIN Brit war hero, 49, locked up in ex-Soviet hell jail after painkillers deemed ‘banned drugs’ faces £60k bill to be freed

A WOUNDED British war hero locked up in the ex-Soviet state of Georgia after his painkillers were branded banned drugs is facing a £60,000 bill to get out of jail.

Ex-Sergeant Matthew Desmond, 49, normally takes a cocktail of powerful drugs every day to ward off spasms caused by spinal injuries suffered in action in Afghanistan.



He was on a motorcycle touring holiday in eastern Europe when he crossed into Georgia and declared his prescription medicines to officials at the border.

But they slung him into a hellhole jail and charged him with importing banned narcotics, warning him he faced a sentence of up to 10 years.



Matthew hopes to walk free on Wednesday after being forced to plead guilty to avoid further agony during extended legal wrangles.

But his distraught family revealed today he faces losing his life savings paying off an expected hefty fine plus legal costs.



His sister Claire-Louise Rough, 43, said: “Matthew will be using his life savings from a career of service to his country to pay for the fine, legal bills and costs which will be £60,000.

“His family has set up a gofundme for those who are sympathetic to Matt’s situation.

The former elite soldier was then denied his prescribed drugs and given only weak painkillers, which took away just 10 per cent of the pain he endures from his war wounds.

And the multi-medal-winning former Para is only now in the process of walking free – after being forced to pay up to £28,200 fine and plead guilty in a plea bargain deal.



Matthew gained legendary status within the ranks after leading firefights in the badlands of Afghanistan’s Helmand Province in 2008 in an area dubbed “The Mouth Of Hell.”

He lost 30 comrades from 2 Para in the most intensive fighting seen since World War II in which 300 Taliban troops were killed and was wounded several times.

But he later retrained and returned as a bomb disposal expert, tackling Taliban roadside bombs on some of the most dangerous missions of the conflict.



His motorcycle tour had taken in 25 countries across Europe without any problem with border authorities until he was held crossing into Georgia from Turkey on April 23.

Matthew’s Georgian lawyer, Jaba Kochlamazashvili, said: “My client served in Iraq and Afghanistan, and is decorated with multiple awards.

“He sustained the spinal injuries that still affect him while serving in Afghanistan during a parachute jump.

“Although we submitted documents in May confirming that he was using these medications for legitimate medical purposes, the prosecution argues that, at the moment he entered Georgia, he did not possess the complete set of required documentation.

“Our position is that since circumstances clearly demonstrate that a person had no criminal intent whatsoever, those circumstances should be taken into account.”



Mr Kochlamazashvili said Mathew, from Nottingham, was found to be carrying a month’s supply of painkilling tablets including buprenorphine, codeine and Pregabalin.

The lawyer added: “These medications were brought into Georgia solely for his personal medical use because of the injuries he sustained.

“Internally at least, the Prosecutor’s Office accepts this argument, which is why they have offered us a plea agreement involving only a fine.



“The difficulty is that Matthew would still have to plead guilty.”

Matthew – enduring daily agony in a cell at grim Gldani Prison- was also denied any means of contacting his family back home for weeks

The hellhole jail – officially known as Penitentiary Establishment No. 8 in capital Tbilisi – was made infamous by leaked footage of prisoners being tortured in 2012.

Mr Kochlamazashvili added: “Matthew’s family were in complete shock and had no idea what was happening.

“Until we became involved, Matthew wasn’t even able to call them. They were left in a complete information vacuum and were deeply distressed.



“Matthew suffers from constant, unbearable pain. He struggles to walk, lie down or even sit comfortably.

“The medication available in prison is very weak and reduces his pain by perhaps ten per cent.

“Nevertheless, he is mentally very resilient and is enduring the situation while hoping for his release.”



Another Georgian lawyer representing Matthew, Giorgi Cherkezia revealed his motorcycle tour of Georgia had been planned to coincide with St George’s Day in April.

The practising Christian was on his way to join in church-led celebrations when he was arrested and jailed.

Mr Cherkezia said”He is in constant pain – he’s suffering. The man is utterly exhausted. Whenever we visit him, he can barely put one foot in front of the other,”.

Lawyers have opted for a costly plea bargain deal fearing Matthew will be unable to endure up to seven more months of legal wrangling without his painkilling meds.

Former army officers who fought alongside decorated former bomb-disposal expert Matthew sent character reference letters to Georgian authorities pleading for mercy.



Former officer, major William Balchin said: “In the 20 years I have known Matthew he has always obeyed the law of the country and been an example for others to follow.

“His decorated military career and lasting legacy amongst his peers is testament to his integrity and character.

“Matthew has deployed to Afghanistan as well as other theatres of war on multiple occasions and was awarded the Meritorious Service Medal (MSM) with the Parachute Regiment.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He is widely regarded as a fantastic soldier.”

Matthew is due to appear at a court hearing in Tbilisi on Wednesday when his lawyers hope he will finally walk free.

News.title: Raging woman bit cop’s BUM and kicked another officer while being arrested over ‘meltdown’ at her home
News.content:
SAVAGE ATTACK Raging woman bit cop’s BUM and kicked another officer while being arrested over ‘meltdown’ at her home

A RAGING woman bit a cop’s bum and kicked another officer while being arrested.

Hannah Metcalfe, 25, sank her teeth into PC Chris Pountain after officers were called to her home.



She also kicked one of his colleagues on the shin and mauled the officer before being handcuffed.

Metcalfe has now pleaded guilty to two charges of assault by beating of an emergency worker.



She avoided jail and was instead handed a 12 month community order with a requirement that she attends up to 25 days of rehabilitation activity days.

Metcalfe was made subject to 30 days of alcohol monitoring and made to pay £100 each in compensation the officers, along with £85 costs.

Crewe Magistrates’ Court was told police had been called to Metcalfe’s home on January 31 following reports of an offence at a nearby property.

Nigel Jones, prosecuting, said: “The defendant’s mood and demeanour were up and down. One moment she was calm and the next turned into a rage.



”As so doing, she kicked out at PC Potts making a connection with his left shin causing him pain and discomfort.

”A police van was requested due to her behaviour but she became aggressive again and had to be restrained on the floor. Whilst on the floor she bit PC Pountain on his bottom. A bite is an unpleasant incident for any individual.

“The aggravating factor is these are assaults on police officers in the execution of their duty. ”

Metcalfe’s lawyer Jim Edwards said his client immediately apologised for her behaviour at the time of her arrest.

He added: ”There is an issue is in relation to a previous partner who is in custody awaiting a trial in October for an allegation against my client.”



The court was told Metcalfe has a history of heavy drinking but this has been “considerably reduced”.

Sentencing, JP Andrew Kerr told her: “You clearly have mental health issues which may have accounted for your behaviour.

”We hope that the rehabilitative aspect of this sentence will form an element of rectitude moving forward preventing you behaving any further as you have done.”

News.title: PMQs LIVE: Keir Starmer set for final PMQs and cabinet as Andy Burnham prepares for No10
News.content:
Outgoing Sir Keir Starmer will take to the despatch box for the last time as Prime Minister later today before he is expected to be succeeded by Andy Burnham next week

Keir Starmer will take part in his final Prime Minister's Questions later today as he prepares to say goodbye to Downing Street.

The outgoing leader will first host farewell talks with his senior ministers at number 10 before taking his last Commons grilling at noon.

Prime Minister-in-waiting Andy Burnham will edge closer to his job tonight as nominations for the Labour leadership formally close on Wednesday. Today, he will face Tory leader Kemi Badenoch and is expected to be hit with tough hand-over questions.

Sir Keir is spending his final days in office highlighting what he sees as his legacy, including his backing of campaigns like the Hillsborough Law and the government's support for Ukraine.

He said: "I’m pleased to have delivered on the promises that I made to many people in this garden, and I’ll make this last promise, which is I will stand with you and walk with you for as long as I’ve got breath in my body.”

News.title: Ann Widdecombe murder probe: Counter Terrorism Police say veteran politician killed in 'targeted attack'
News.content:
Latest police update - in full

Yesterday a police spokesperson said: "The murder investigation into the death of Ann Widdecombe is continuing today, with further details provided by Counter Terrorism Policing.

A 28-year-old man arrested in connection with this incident remains under arrest on suspicion of commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism, as we well as on suspicion of murder. A warrant of further detention has been granted, which means the suspect can now be held for questioning for up to seven days under the Terrorism Act.

Head of National Counter Terrorism, Laurence Taylor, provided the following update: “The shocking death of Ann Widdecombe has very much dominated the headlines since the news first broke last week.

“This incident has had a deeply distressing impact on Ann Widdecombe’s family, and we are doing all we can to support them, alongside our colleagues in Devon and Cornwall Police.

“The thoughts of everyone at Counter Terrorism Policing are with them at what is a very challenging time. As we confirmed yesterday, Counter Terrorism Policing South East are now leading the investigation.

“This is due to new information and evidence coming to light following the arrest of a 28-year-old man on Saturday in South Yorkshire. It is clear that this was a targeted attack. We are still working to understand the extent of any planning or preparation, and the motivation that sits behind it.

“Extensive searches have taken place at an address in Rotherham and scenes remain in place as that activity continues.

“This is a complex investigation and there are multiple lines of enquiry that we are pursuing expeditiously including digital forensic examinations. I am very aware of the significant levels of public interest in this case, given that Miss Widdecombe was such a high-profile political and public figure, and familiar to many.

“I do not intend to address every bit of speculation we have seen, but I would like to use this opportunity to remind the public that investigations of this type are complex, and new information can emerge as officers progress their enquiries. We intend to release further information when it’s available and appropriate to do so.

“Please allow us to do our job, thoroughly, and carefully, and think before sharing unverified information. It is important to remember that this is a murder investigation, following a brutal attack on a 78-year-old lady in her own home. I want to ensure that our work is conducted sensitively and considers the impact of what has happened.

“I would like to end by reassuring all of those who knew, or knew of, Ann Widdecombe that our excellent teams of investigators are working incredibly hard, with the aim of securing justice for her and her family. If you have any information that you think might help us with this investigation, please contact the police.”

Any relevant information, images or footage can be reported via the Major Incident Public Portal https://mipp.police.uk/operation/50DC26S51-PO1 or to Devon and Cornwall Police on 101.

Information can also be passed anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555111.

News.title: Woman dragged to ground in horror tube rape attempt as police launch CCTV appeal
News.content:
Woman dragged to ground in horror tube rape attempt as police launch CCTV appeal

A woman fought off an alleged attacker after she was dragged to the floor on a tube, as police released CCTV images of a man they believe could help with their investigation

View 3 Images Police have appealed for help identifying a man they want to speak to following the alleged attack (Image: British Transport Police/PA Wire)

Police released CCTV images of a man they want to speak to after a woman was allegedly dragged to the floor and attacked on the tube.

The woman had been travelling alone on a Bakerloo Line service between Waterloo and Lambeth North when she was allegedly targeted in an horrific attack at about 11.40pm on Saturday, July 11.

In a statement, British Transport Police said a man approached her before exposing himself, he then pulled the woman to the floor and attempted to rape her.

The woman fought back before escaping the tube at Lambeth North station, where immediately she alerted station staff.

View 3 Images Police have not accused the man pictured of any offence (Image: BRITISH TRANSPORT POLICE)

Police said the man involved in the horrific incident remained on the tube and later got off at Elephant and Castle Underground station.

Detectives released CCTV images of a man they want to identify because they believe he may have information that could assist their investigation. Police have not accused the man pictured of any offence

An investigation has been ongoing to track the man's movements and they believe he was at Oxford Circus Underground station before the incident and at Piccadilly Circus Underground station afterwards.

BTP Detective Sergeant Krishan Appannah said: “Our officers are supporting the victim following this horrific incident. We understand incidents of this nature are deeply concerning for the public and we’re appealing to them directly to help us identify the man in the CCTV footage. One line of enquiry is that he may be homeless.

News.title: Aldi axes bestselling item from shelves in act of 'solidarity' on July 15
News.content:
Aldi axes bestselling item from shelves in act of 'solidarity' on July 15

The budget supermarket has removed all stock from the shelves with a sign explaining why

View 2 Images Aldi axes the wine from shelves ahead of World Cup showdown (Image: Aldi )

In a show of patriotic solidarity, a sign has appeared in an Aldi store announcing it has removed one of its bestselling items from shelves. The decision to remove stock from the supermarket has been noticed by shoppers online, who have shared their opinions on Instagram.

‌



Ahead of tonight's (July 15) FIFA World Cup 2026 game, where England will go up against Argentina, Aldi has temporarily axed its popular Argentinian Malbec from shelves as a lighthearted joke. England's highly anticipated semi-final clash against Argentina will determine whether the Three Lions players will make it through to the final showdown on Sunday, July 19.

‌



According to Aldi’s latest Instagram post, shoppers visiting the store's wine aisle today will find empty shelves where the popular red wine usually sits. The wine has been replaced by a sign explaining why it has vanished.

‌



The sign reads: "We have removed our Argentinian Malbec from the shelves in solidarity ahead of the game tomorrow." At the bottom, it adds: "It’s coming home!"

An Aldi spokesperson said: "Whether it's a tactical substitution or the ultimate superstition, the sign encourages shoppers to bench their usual Argentinian reds for alternative bottles to toast Thomas Tuchel’s men tonight. Those looking to toast to England’s success this evening night can pick up any of Aldi’s non-Argentinian wines in store now."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



On Instagram, Aldi uploaded an image of the sign after a customer spotted it in their local store. Aldi responded to say: "The only thing NOT coming home is your nice bottle of vino (soz x)."

In the caption, Aldi added: "If this doesn’t help us win, we don’t know what will." The post has since gone viral, with more than 15k likes and hundreds of comments from fans.

In the comment section, one person said: "Your creative team are brilliant!" Another wrote: "Now I respect Aldi even more." A third put: "Patriotism before Profit. Well done." Another claimed: "Worked for us when @Greggs_official removed all Mexican flavoured items!!"

‌

Remember to drink responsibly. The UK Chief Medical Officers recommend drinking no more than 14 units a week, spreading this evenly across three or more days, and having several drink-free days each week.

What time is the England vs Argentina World Cup semi-final?

Tonight, on Wednesday, July 15, 2026, the World Cup semi-final between England and Argentina starts at 8pm. The game will take place at the Atlanta Stadium (Mercedes-Benz Stadium) in Georgia, USA.
